The relation between the selling price of a car (in $1,000) and its age (in years) is estimated from a random sample of cars of a specific model. The relation is given by the following formula: Selling price = 15.9 – 0.983 (age) Which of the following can we conclude from this equation?
Option A: For every year the car gets older, the selling price goes down by approximately 9.83 percent.
Option B: A new car costs on the average $9,830.
Option C: For every year the car gets older, the selling price drops by approximately $1,590.
Option D: For every year the car gets older, the selling price drops by approximately $983.
